name: CA-43
label: Safe D

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Maxine Waters running for re-election
Challenger Cristian Morales has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Waters holds a heavily Democratic Los Angeles-area seat with a +27 partisan lean, has a long incumbency advantage, and outraised her little-known challenger, who reports no fundraising. Markets price her around 96%, and no polls or ratings suggest the race is competitive.
model.watch: Any sign of a serious challenger fundraising push or a scandal involving Waters could narrow the margin, though history suggests low-turnout general elections here stay safely Democratic.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maxine Waters, a longtime Democratic incumbent, is seeking re-election in a Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by about 27 points. She advanced to the general election against Republican Cristian Morales, a little-known challenger who has reported no fundraising, while Waters has raised roughly $864,000 and holds cash on hand. Prediction markets give Waters about a 96% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture. Waters is heavily favored to win another term, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile contest rather than any genuine competitive threat.
